texts.preamble: Ravi vs The State Of Kerala on 11 February, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Thursday, The 11Th Day Of February 2016/22Nd Magha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 4430 of 2006 ( ) --------------------------------- Cra 29/2002 of Addl. Sessions Court, Fast Track(Adhoc)-Iv, Thiruvananthapuram St 179/1995 Of The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Thiruvananthapuram Revision Petitioner/Appellant/Accused:: --------------------------------------- Ravi, Aged 44, S/O. Kumara Pillai, T.C.20/1124, Karamana Ward Thiruvananthapuram. By Advs.Sri.Kottoor B.Gopalakrishna Pillai Sri.R.T.Pradeep Respondent(S)/Respondent/Complainant:: --------------------------------- The State Of Kerala, Represented By The Director General Of Prosecution High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam. By Public Prosecutor Sri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 11-02-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Scl. Ravi vs The State Of Kerala on 11 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15044371/ 1 B. Sudheendra Kumar, J. ------------------------------------- Crl.R.P.No. 4430 of 2006 -------------------------------------- Dated this the 11th day of February, 2016 Order
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 18.8.1994 at about 11.30 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 600 gram of compounded asafoetida from the revision petitioner. After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis. Ext. P4 report of the public analyst would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and was therefore adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P16 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P4 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P4 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and Ravi vs The State Of Kerala on 11 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15044371/ 2 found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
